decision: User adopted the binary-collapsed scoring convention for the MS qualification gate (SEMANTIC_ABSTAIN merged into NOT_SUITABLE for exact-match gate purposes only; the underlying review instrument still emits full 3-way final_suitability, and SEMANTIC_ABSTAIN remains a real, separately-tracked outcome downstream) and approved GPT-5.6 (primary) + Claude Haiku 4.5 (challenger) as the qualified reviewer pairing.

precedent.summary: Two independent human clinician reviewers on a comparable task: strict 3-way Cohen's kappa .4854 (below its own .75 gate); binary-collapsed kappa .6175 (production-acceptable range). Same collapse logic applied here.

external_corroboration: Follow-up emotional-support strategy-annotation study: Fleiss' kappa ~.458 on a comparable categorical task, nearly identical to this project's own .4854.
General LLM-judge-agreement literature: human-human pairwise agreement only 69-75% (mean 72%), below the 91.7%-100% this gate demanded on a harder 3-way task.

ES-MemEval (arXiv:2602.01885, the actual target benchmark): does not attempt fine-grained subjective suitability labeling; QA/abstention are grounded in objectively-checkable constructed event timelines, and the one genuinely subjective task (dialogue quality) uses a single coarse LLM-judge scale, not multi-reviewer 3-way consensus.

retired_challenger.reason: Fails the qualification gate even under the binary-collapsed convention; its errors are real USE/DO_NOT_USE direction flips, not boundary-precision misses, so the scoring-granularity fix does not rescue it. Ruled out separately: thinking budget is not the cause (round 4 null result).

known_open_gap_not_blocking.description: Vague/content-free candidate text over-interpreted as a specific claim. Shared across Gemini and Claude Haiku (only GPT-5.6 got it right); not Gemini-specific. Worth a targeted prompt tightening later but does not block proceeding to the formal 201-item pass, since it is a single item pattern, not a systemic failure of the qualified pairing.

governs.formal_201_item_pass_consensus_rule: binary_collapsed_exact_agreement_only (same convention applied for consistency; disagreement/abstain-vs-not-suitable-split stays unlabeled, matching the existing exact-consensus-only philosophy)
